title: A Robot That Knows How Lost It Is: Dead Reckoning, Beacon Fixes, and a Fence Buffer That Is Only as Good as the Drift It Assumes

questions.question: The wheel base is 5 percent out. What does it cost when driving straight?
options: 5 percent of the distance
Nothing: it only divides the difference between the wheels
The heading, which drifts 5 percent
About a metre in 30
questions.explanation: The wheel base only enters where the wheels' distances differ. Going straight they are equal, and the error was 0.00 at 10, 20 and 30 m.

questions.question: A wheel 1 percent big gave 1.66 m at 10 m. What was the error at 20 m and 30 m?
options: 3.32 and 4.98: in proportion to the distance
6.55 and 14.49: about four and nine times, since the error goes as the square of the distance
1.66 at both: the error does not grow
0.83 and 0.55: fixes average it down
questions.explanation: A wheel that is a little big turns the robot steadily, so the heading error grows with distance and the position error with its square.

questions.question: Why do fixes every 2 s leave an error of 1.42 m when each fix is good to 0.1 m?
options: The filter is tuned too slowly
The beacon's 0.1 m is optimistic
The error is set by the time between fixes: the drift between them, and the fix does not correct the heading, which is what is wrong
The wheel is 10 percent big
questions.explanation: A fix resets the position and leaves the heading wrong, so the drift starts again at once. How far it gets is set by how long until the next fix.

questions.question: A fence on the believed position was given no buffer. What happened to the robot whose truth left the corridor after 9.6 m?
options: It stopped at the edge
It slowed as it neared the edge
It turned back toward the axis
It never stopped: the belief stays on the axis, so the fence never trips, and the robot ended at y = -18.3 m
questions.explanation: The fence was checked against where the robot believed it was. That belief stayed in the middle of the corridor while the robot left it.

questions.question: Which assumed drifts stopped the robot before the truth left the corridor?
options: 0.20 and 0.40 m per metre: 0.05 and 0.10 stopped it after the truth was outside, and the real drift at the edge was 0.156 and growing
All four
None of them
Only 0.05, the smallest
questions.explanation: By the time the truth reached the edge it had drifted 1.5 m in 9.6 m, and the rate was rising. A buffer built on less than that stops too late.

questions.question: What do fixes every 5 s add to the safety argument?
options: Range: with the same assumed drift the robot went 8.7 m before it had to stop, against 5.1 m without
Safety: with fixes no buffer is needed
A smaller stopping distance
Nothing measurable
questions.explanation: The buffer grows with the distance since the last fix. Fixes keep that distance short, so the robot can go further before the buffer fills the corridor.
